topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and the lecture’s focus
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing its focus on cancer evolution, cell of origin, and the microenvironment, and by stating its learning aims.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic change in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics explain how changes in a cell’s heritable state can promote its expansion or transformation during cancer evolution.

topics.label: Cell of origin and stem-like hierarchies in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how a cell’s position in a tissue hierarchy and its stem-like properties can shape cancer development.

topics.label: Microenvironmental influences on cancer growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how signals and support from the microenvironment can enable cancer cells to initiate, sustain, or expand tumor growth.

topics.label: Methods for studying cancer evolution and cell interactions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes sequencing and spatial methods used to investigate tumor-cell states and their interactions within tissues.

topics.label: Integrating mutation, cell properties, and environment in cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how mutations, cellular states, and environmental conditions combine to make malignant growth possible.

topics.label: Lecture close and preview of the next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic ends the lecture and identifies therapy as the subject of the next meeting.
